one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, sampling-aware audit protocol claiming that retrieved-experience memory and GEPA-optimized instructions are the same kind of device — distribution-concentration, not information-addition — such that each buys pass@1 by deleting solvable instances via mode shift (not sharpening), stacking them compounds the loss while sub-adding the gain, and the only harvestable complementarity is across rollouts rather than across prompt slots.
closest_prior_work: Two threats. (1) arXiv 2605.28224 ("When Does Memory Help Multi-Trajectory Inference for Tool-Use LLM Agents?"), which the proposal itself concedes owns the memory-side causal story in the same regime; what survives is genuinely narrower than the Title advertises — coverage bookkeeping, a temperature control, and the optimizer half. (2) The training-time collapse literature (2509.06941, 2509.04784) plus GEPA/MIPROv2's own objective: a search that greedily maximizes single-sample validation accuracy over a fixed sampler is, by construction, a concentration device. Predicting that O1 loses pass@k is close to definitionally true, so the optimizer half — the part the proposal makes its spine — is an unsurprising positive, not a discovery. The portfolio corollary is weaker still: prompt/condition ensembling to raise coverage is folklore in the repeated-sampling literature (their own cited 2505.12938 runs this direction), and Prediction 9 is nearly entailed by Prediction 6 — if A1 and O1 concentrate onto modes with mean JSD ≥ 0.4 and each crosses over by k=8, the union of their solve sets beating any single arm is arithmetic, not evidence.
strongest_objection: The coverage decomposition is biased toward its own predicted answer by the instance-selection rule. Risk factor 2 selects the test pool to have unconditioned pass@1 in the 30–60% band. NEW is defined as "A0 never solves in n=16, treatment sometimes does" — at a true A0 rate of 0.30 the probability of zero successes in 16 draws is ~0.003, so the NEW cell is emptied by the sampling design, while LOST ("treatment never solves in 16") is thresholded on the treatment arm, which the filter does not constrain at all. The filter is applied to A0 only, so the decomposition is structurally asymmetric: Prediction 2 (NEW < 4% of the test set, LOST/NEW ≥ 2) is close to guaranteed by the pool construction plus n=16 resolution regardless of whether memory or the optimizer removes any solution. The Jeffreys posterior and split-half checks quantify the noise in the labels but do not touch the selection asymmetry that generates the predicted ratio. Second, mutually reinforcing: the prechecks demand a ≥5-point (memory) and ≥3-point (GEPA) pass@1 gain and say "we enrich the bank / extend the GEPA budget until it passes" on a 150-instance dev split. That is selecting each component for maximal single-sample concentration on dev — precisely the property whose consequences are then measured on test — and it directly contradicts the track's own measured starting position (memory fixed zero and broke six to seven; the optimizer's gain was redistribution, not accuracy). The conditions under which the study runs at all are the conditions that manufacture its conclusion. Third, the paper's actual centre is underpowered by its own arithmetic: stated SE is ~1.7 points on a single paired pass@k difference (MDE ~4.5 points), yet Prediction 7 is a three-arm difference-of-differences with a 2-point slack and Prediction 8 asks for a 2-point O3-over-O2 gap and a 0.1 JSD shift. A contrast of contrasts carries roughly 2.5–3 points of SE here, so the coupling claims — the half the proposal says degrades gracefully into the contribution — cannot be resolved by this design in either direction.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Stop conditioning the pool on A0. Either select instances by a conditioning-blind criterion (e.g. pooled solve rate across all arms, or stratified sampling over the full difficulty range) or abandon the NEW/LOST thresholds as primary and make the headline a continuous, symmetric statistic: the paired shift in per-instance solve probability (Δ log-odds, or the signed mass moving off/onto zero under the Jeffreys posterior), reported over the unfiltered test set. Report NEW/LOST as a secondary readout with the selection-induced floor stated explicitly. 2) Add a temperature-matched A0 arm alongside A4. As written, if A4 fails to restore coverage, "memory shifted the mode" is confounded with "hot decoding degrades ReAct tool-call coherence"; only A0 at the same temperature separates them, and this is cheap. 3) Restore the top-3 injection-volume arm. The token-matched decoy A3 spans content, not dosage, and the track's own prior result names volume as the causal lever; without a dose axis the finding may be "more conditioning tokens concentrate," which is a dosage story, not a common currency. 4) Fix the precheck before looking at anything: pre-register the enrichment procedure and its stopping rule, or drop the gate and report what a standard ExpeL-style bank and a fixed GEPA budget actually do, including the case where the honest answer is the track's own null. 5) Power the coupling contrasts — restate Predictions 7 and 8 at ≥5 points, or reallocate rollouts from the descriptive arms to O2/O3 so a difference-of-differences is detectable.
missing_baseline: GEPA run against a multi-sample objective — candidate selection on pass@4 (or on solve-set coverage) instead of single-sample validation accuracy, then pushed through the identical coverage pipeline. The Related Work section diagnoses the problem as the optimizer's objective being sampling-unaware, but no arm changes the objective, so the plan cannot distinguish "prompt optimization is intrinsically a concentration device" (the paper's thesis) from "pass@1-greedy search concentrates, and a two-line change to the selection metric fixes it" — the latter is both more likely and cheaper to test than the portfolio machinery, and a reviewer will demand it because the proposal itself supplies the argument for it. Secondarily, the cut top-3 injection-volume arm (the dose control the track's own prior results single out) and MIPROv2 as a second optimizer, without which "prompt optimization" means "GEPA's reflective operator."
preprint_collision: Unusually honest and above the norm for this exercise: it names a genuine partial collision (2605.28224), concedes the memory-side claim to it rather than arguing it away, reorganizes the proposal around what survives, states the remaining delta concretely (solve-set measurement, diversity-matched control, falsifiable decoy prediction, no optimizer), and admits an exhausted budget with three uncharacterized titles and no OpenReview sweep. That earns credit. But the check is thin exactly where the surviving novelty lives. The searches cover memory-and-diversity and training-time collapse thoroughly, and the optimizer side is represented only by MIPROv2/GEPA themselves — there is no search at all for prompt or instruction optimization evaluated under pass@k, for diversity- or coverage-aware prompt search, or for few-shot demonstrations reducing solve-set coverage in code/agent generation, and only one lexical-diversity ICL citation (2404.16807) stands in for that whole area. The portfolio corollary is likewise unsearched: heterogeneous prompt/condition ensembling to raise pass@k is established practice in the repeated-sampling literature and the proposal cites only 2505.12938 as a "counterpoint" rather than as a coverage-ensembling precedent. So both halves the proposal now claims as its own — optimizer-as-concentrator and the portfolio fix — rest on an unsearched novelty claim, which is a weakness, not a neutral. Also, the surviving contribution is now one preprint's follow-up analysis away from being fully scooped, and the proposal's own Risk 1 concedes this.
